title: backlog.py tidy --path removes one recorded leftover, so a session can remove its own worktree without tidying every other session's
goal: `backlog.py tidy --path PATH` (repeatable) keeps only the recorded leftovers at those paths, listed or, with `--apply`, removed under the same `safe_to_remove` verdict as every tidy row, so a session removes its own worktree and no other's; a path no record names exits 2 naming it

run:
import os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
R = os.getcwd(); T = os.path.realpath(tempfile.mkdtemp())
env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("GIT_")}
env["KB_COORD_STORE"] = os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite")
def sh(*a, cwd=T):
    return subprocess.run(a, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
O = os.path.join(T, "origin.git"); K = os.path.join(T, "clone")
sh("git", "init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", O)
sh("git", "clone", "-q", O, K)
shutil.copy(os.path.join(R, "backlog.json"), K); os.makedirs(os.path.join(K, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
sh("git", "add", ".", cwd=K)
sh("git", "-c", "user.email=a@b", "-c", "user.name=n", "commit", "-q", "-m", "b", cwd=K)
sh("git", "push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main", cwd=K)
sh("git", "fetch", "-q", cwd=K)
bl = lambda *a: sh(sys.executable, os.path.join(R, "_tools", "backlog.py"), "--root", K, *a, cwd=K)
paths = {}
for n in ("a", "b"):
    p = os.path.join(K, ".claude", "worktrees", "review-" + n)
    sh("git", "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", p, "origin/main", cwd=K)
    bl("own", p, "--class", "worktree", "--sprint", "SP-aaaaaaaa")
    paths[n] = p
if not all(os.path.isdir(p) for p in paths.values()):
    print("check broken: the planted worktrees were not made"); sys.exit(2)
problems = []
dry = bl("tidy", "--path", paths["a"], "--older-than", "0")
if dry.returncode != 0 or "review-a" not in dry.stdout or "review-b" in dry.stdout:
    problems.append("tidy --path A (no --apply) does not list A alone: exit %d %s %s" % (dry.returncode, dry.stdout[-300:], dry.stderr[-200:]))
if not os.path.isdir(paths["a"]):
    problems.append("tidy --path without --apply removed A")
r = bl("tidy", "--path", paths["a"], "--older-than", "0", "--apply")
if r.returncode != 0 or os.path.isdir(paths["a"]):
    problems.append("tidy --path A --apply did not remove A: exit %d %s %s" % (r.returncode, r.stdout[-300:], r.stderr[-200:]))
if not os.path.isdir(paths["b"]):
    problems.append("tidy --path A --apply removed B too")
dirty = os.path.join(paths["b"], "planted-change.txt")
open(dirty, "w").write("x\n")
d = bl("tidy", "--path", paths["b"], "--older-than", "0", "--apply")
if not os.path.isdir(paths["b"]):
    problems.append("tidy --path --apply removed a worktree with an untracked file")
u = bl("tidy", "--path", os.path.join(T, "not-recorded"), "--older-than", "0")
if u.returncode != 2:
    problems.append("a --path no record names exits %d, not 2: %s" % (u.returncode, (u.stdout + u.stderr)[-200:]))
print("\n".join(problems) or "ok")
sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)

clauses.clause: `backlog.py tidy --path PATH` (repeatable) keeps only the recorded leftovers at those paths, listed or, with `--apply`, removed under the same `safe_to_remove` verdict as every tidy row, so a session removes its own worktree and no other's
a path no record names exits 2 naming it

notes: Operator request 2026-10-26: `.claude/settings.json` denies `git worktree remove` to agents (kept), and `tidy --apply` removes every safe leftover of every session at once, so a session could not remove its own reviewer worktree. The deny stays; the remedy is this filter on the tool route with all of tidy's checks. The close's kept line is in bl_close.py (`left for tidy --apply`). No suite test: the check is a planted run.
